Research Buddy

A question-answering assistant that grounds responses in uploaded academic papers through retrieval, embeddings and focused context.

The problem

Finding an answer in a long paper means locating the right section, understanding its context and checking the wording. A general language model may answer from prior knowledge without using the document. I wanted the answer path to begin with the paper itself.

How I built it

The application accepts a research paper, parses its text and splits it into overlapping chunks. I create vector embeddings for those chunks, store them for similarity search and retrieve the most relevant passages for a question. LangChain connects that retrieval step to the language model.

PDF upload→Parse & chunk→Embed→Retrieve→Grounded answer

My engineering decisions

  • Chunk overlap preserves context across section boundaries.
  • Similarity search narrows the material sent to the model so the answer is based on relevant passages.
  • The answer prompt restricts generation to retrieved content, improving traceability to the document.

Result & next step

The working application lets a reader upload a paper and ask natural-language questions about it. The public repository contains the application and retrieval code. A future evaluation could score answer faithfulness and retrieval quality on a labeled question set; I have not published those metrics for this version.
